stem: Meena is camping with her family near Jaipur. At night, she wants to find the North direction using the stars. She can see the Big Dipper and the Little Dipper patterns in the sky. Which method will correctly help Meena find North?

options.text: She should look at the brightest star in the Big Dipper, because the brightest star always marks North.
She should find the Pole Star (Polaris), which is part of the Little Dipper and appears fixed in the North direction.
She should follow the Big Dipper, because the Big Dipper itself points to the South direction.
She should wait until the stars move, because the Pole Star keeps changing its position during the night.

teacher.key_rationale: Polaris (the Pole Star) is part of the Little Dipper and appears stationary in the northern sky, so locating it identifies North. Options A and C misapply the Big Dipper, and D is wrong because the Pole Star appears fixed.
